What is the difference between a camera dictionary and Google Lens?

Google Lens and a camera dictionary can both help with text on a printed page. Choose according to the result you need: translating a passage, copying text, searching for information, or reading a dictionary entry for one word.

Lens is a general visual search tool with text and translation features. Its available actions depend on the app, device and language. For a long passage, compare its text-translation workflow with your needs before choosing a dedicated dictionary.

Booktionary focuses on a word in a paper book. Hold the centre ring over it to open a dictionary definition. Dismiss the panel to continue reading or scan another word. Installed dictionaries work offline, with English included and 23 additional book dictionaries available to download.

For English books, optional packs add word equivalents in 24 target languages. Translated definitions are also available for 19 supported destinations on iOS 18 or later after downloading the required language files. Booktionary does not translate a whole page. Recognition and dictionary coverage vary, so try a word that matters to your reading rather than assuming every tool gives the same result.

Try a word from your book

  1. Choose the book language. Download its dictionary if needed.
  2. Tap Start reading and allow camera access.
  3. In good light, hold the centre ring over the printed word for about a second.
  4. Read the definition. Swipe the panel away to return to the camera and your book.

See the app, all supported languages and download requirements.
